solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicatorNotes.retreating: a retreat goes backwards, so the letters read right to left

blocks.note: TA = Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

annotation.surface: Green recruits falling back in the middle of a battle.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole two-piece string turns round, not each piece on its own. The Territorial Army is the British army's part-time reserve, hence 'volunteers'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a nation at war is engaged in combat.

blocks.note: 'I can' = 'I am able', so Can gives AM ABLE
I stays as itself, slipped between AM and ABLE

annotation.surface: A shy question: may I be your friend?
annotation.walkthrough: The trick is turning a statement's verb into a question: 'I can' becomes 'Can I?', and 'I am able' becomes 'Am I able?', so the I lands in the middle.
annotation.definitionFit: Amiable means friendly, behaving like a friend.

blocks.note: the surface offers the heavy metal; the setter means the verb, to be in charge
the surface offers sacks; 'bags' is old British slang for loose trousers, so this means wearing them

annotation.surface: A question about something heavy, the metal lead, packed into sacks.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'lead' as the verb to be in charge and 'bags' as British slang for trousers: to lead while wearing bags is to wear the trousers, i.e. be the one in charge.
annotation.definitionFit: The person who wears the trousers is the one who leads in a household.

indicatorNotes.say: say asks you to go by the sound of the word

blocks.note: a demolished building has been razed, levelled to the ground

annotation.walkthrough: RAZED and RAISED sound identical but mean opposites: one building has gone up, the other has come down.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to raise a wall or a barn is to build it.

entries.clue: Hard work and drink as a minor diversion (9)

annotation.surface: Someone taking a break from hard work with a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Minor' means a child here: hopscotch is a playground game, a diversion for minors, not a small one.
annotation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a children's hopping game, an amusement for minors.

entries.clue: Number of staff supplied by chief nobleman (9)

annotation.surface: An aristocrat providing the servants for a household.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's 'staff' sounds like servants lent by a lord, but the definition is the modern business word for how many people a firm employs.
annotation.definitionFit: A firm's headcount is the number of people it employs.

entries.clue: Do a balancing act with increased salary (3,2)

blocks.note: up = increased, as in 'prices are up'

annotation.surface: A tightrope walker performing after getting a pay rise.
annotation.walkthrough: The balancing act is not a circus trick but settling an account: paying up brings the balance to zero.
annotation.definitionFit: To pay up is to settle what you owe, balancing the books.

indicatorNotes.Heard: heard tells you to go by what the words sound like

blocks.note: a ship's sailors are its crew, and to chant is to sing

annotation.surface: Passengers overhearing the crew singing aboard the liner QE2.
annotation.walkthrough: Said aloud, CREW SING gives the answer. The QE2 (Queen Elizabeth 2) was a famous British ocean liner used for cruises; the question mark marks it as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the QE2 was a cruise liner, so being on board meant taking a cruise.

annotation.definitionNote: 'to be going on with' is an adjectival phrase, as in 'enough to be going on with'

blocks.note: serving for now, until something better turns up
a ticket or passport is what you board, or go on, a journey with

annotation.surface: A question about stopgap passports and tickets.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful reading: a ticket or passport is something you go on (a journey) with.
annotation.definitionFit: Something to be going on with serves for now, until something better comes along.

entries.clue: Keep complaining about one’s first dart (7)

indicatorNotes.first: take the first letter of the word it follows

annotation.surface: A grumbler who keeps moaning about their first go at darts.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface puts us in a pub game of darts, but the dart here is the whaler's weapon; 'one's first' means the first letter of the word one.
annotation.definitionFit: A harpoon is a barbed spear thrown or fired, a kind of dart.

annotation.surface: A penniless inventor claiming credit for anaesthetic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without capital' means lower case: small i is the mathematicians' symbol for the square root of minus one. NUMBER is read as numb-er, not the counting word.
annotation.definitionFit: Lower-case i denotes the imaginary unit, the basic imaginary number.

indicatorNotes.swapped: the two pieces change places, so the second written comes first

blocks.note: a ram is a butter, one that butts

annotation.surface: At a farm show, a prize-winning ram traded for a cow.
annotation.walkthrough: BUTTER is read as butt-er, a butting animal. Buttercup is a traditional name for a cow, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is the traditional pet name for a dairy cow, as Rover is for a dog.

entries.clue: Play it again, Sam? Initially, say no (5)

annotation.surface: The famous Casablanca line, followed by a refusal.
annotation.walkthrough: A segno is the sign in sheet music marking where a repeat starts. The clue borrows the misquoted Casablanca line 'Play it again, Sam'.
annotation.definitionFit: The segno sign tells the player to go back and play a passage again.

annotation.surface: A student reading English and doing very well at it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Studies' is a verb here, looks at closely, not a noun for a course.
annotation.definitionFit: To eye something is to study it closely.

blocks.note: a pension is a small European boarding house

annotation.surface: A traveller asking where to stay in South America.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stay' is the legal sense, as in a stay of execution, not a holiday. 'South American' must be split into two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal sense: a court's stay halts proceedings or a sentence for a time.

blocks.note: handed round, as leaflets or exam papers are
the surface suggests card suits or a fainting fit; the setter means the digging tools handed round

annotation.surface: Garden tools being handed round to a work party.
annotation.walkthrough: Spades handed out have been passed out; the phrase more often means fainted, and a solver thinking of card suits is further led astray.
annotation.definitionFit: To pass out is to distribute, so spades handed round were passed out.

entries.clue: One eating ice-cream right to swallow whole (8)

indicatorNotes.to swallow: the first piece takes the second inside it, as a mouth swallows food

annotation.surface: Someone eating an ice cream and wanting to gulp it down whole.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures someone gulping down a dessert, but 'swallow' only tells one piece to take another inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: A consumer is one who consumes, i.e. eats.

entries.clue: She is a sort to go flying (3,7)

annotation.definition: She is a sort to go flying

indicatorNotes.to go flying: letters sent flying land in a new order

annotation.surface: A description of a woman who works on planes.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: an air hostess is indeed a sort of woman who goes flying.
annotation.definitionFit: An air hostess is a woman whose job takes her flying.

annotation.surface: A defendant's version of events already heard in court.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay, not a possessive.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the courtroom: the person charged and on trial.

annotation.surface: A reporter who grew up to become a good one.
annotation.walkthrough: ED, short for editor, is the crossword's standard journalist.
annotation.definitionFit: Aged means matured, like cheese or wine.

entries.clue: Drives away or is parking in reversing snow vehicle (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the first pieces go inside the vehicle
indicatorNotes.reversing: a reversing vehicle goes backwards, so its letters read right to left

blocks.note: P = parking, as on road signs

annotation.surface: A driver either leaves or parks a backing snowmobile.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drives' looks like motoring, matching the vehicle, but the definition means chases off. The reversal happens first, then the insertion.
annotation.definitionFit: To dispel doubts is to drive them away.

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing labels
a cove is a small bay

annotation.walkthrough: The same word does two jobs: the first Bay is a recess in a room, the second is a stretch of coast.
annotation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recess in a wall, like a bay.

blocks.note: irons are one kind of golf stick, so this is a definition by example
one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards

annotation.surface: Pressing a suit, perhaps with irons.
annotation.walkthrough: Irons are golf clubs, not household appliances, and the suit is one of the four in a pack of cards.
annotation.definitionFit: Clubs is one of the four card suits; irons are a kind of golf club.

entries.clue: Houses or new digs rebuilt around lakes (9)

indicatorNotes.rebuilt: rebuilt = put back together in a new arrangement
indicatorNotes.around: the rearranged letters go around the lakes

blocks.note: L = lake, doubled for the plural

annotation.surface: Moving to a new home rebuilt beside some lakes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Digs' is British slang for lodgings, which suits the housing surface. The anagram of NEW DIGS wraps around LL.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name places where people live.

entries.clue: Detective seizes hot pants in India (5)

indicatorNotes.seizes: the first piece grabs the second and holds it inside

annotation.surface: A detective grabbing some stolen trousers in India.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hot' reads as stolen goods in the surface. A dhoti is a cloth wrapped round the waist and legs, worn by men in India.
annotation.definitionFit: A dhoti is the traditional Indian men's garment serving as trousers.

entries.clue: Obsolete engine to come alive most surprisingly (5,10)

indicatorNotes.surprisingly: the letters end up in an unexpected order

annotation.surface: An old engine being restored and coming back to life against the odds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Most' belongs to the fodder even though it reads as part of 'most surprisingly'.
annotation.definitionFit: Steam locomotives are engines long superseded by diesel and electric.

entries.clue: I had back injury ending in all-out seizure (9)

indicatorNotes.ending in: take the final letter of the next word

annotation.surface: Someone with a bad back after a violent seizure.
annotation.walkthrough: Distraint is the legal seizure of goods to settle a debt, not a medical fit, which is where the surface points.
annotation.definitionFit: Distraint is the seizing of property to force payment of a debt.

entries.clue: A little like those guiding beliefs (5)

indicatorNotes.A little: only a little of the phrase is used: a run of letters inside it

annotation.surface: A few people sharing the same principles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A little' reads as 'somewhat like' in the surface, but it tells you to take a small run of letters from the words that follow.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the characteristic spirit and values that steer a group or institution.
